blocks.text: Trading violations

blocks.raw:
> ## 📋 Regulatory update: Pattern day trading rule changes
>
> **Effective June 4, 2026** — [FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10](https://us.list-manage.com/S4IFLOPKsEJ?e=7f7ca5a638\&c2id=b54217449f03970bad1aa4800cfacc5f)
blocks.text: 📋 Regulatory update: Pattern day trading rule changesEffective June 4, 2026 — FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10

blocks.raw: As a result of FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10, the monitoring and restricting of pattern day trading will be retired. These changes are effective **June 4, 2026** and include the following:
blocks.text: As a result of FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10, the monitoring and restricting of pattern day trading will be retired. These changes are effective June 4, 2026 and include the following:

blocks.raw:
| What's Changing       | Details                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **$25,000 Minimum**   | The hard equity gate required to day trade is being removed                                  |
| **Trade Counters**    | The "4 trades in 5 days" logic is now obsolete                                               |
| **Account Flagging**  | Accounts will no longer be labeled "Pattern Day Trader" or restricted from day trading       |
| **Day Trading Calls** | The day trading leverage calculation is replaced by standard maintenance margin requirements |

rows: The hard equity gate required to day trade is being removed
The "4 trades in 5 days" logic is now obsolete
Accounts will no longer be labeled "Pattern Day Trader" or restricted from day trading
The day trading leverage calculation is replaced by standard maintenance margin requirements

blocks.raw: ## What's new: Intraday margin
blocks.text: What's new: Intraday margin

blocks.raw: While the old "day trade count" is gone, the focus shifts to a more dynamic metric called the **Intraday Margin Level (IML)**. Instead of checking account balances solely at end of day, the new rule requires monitoring of a customer account's highest margin deficiency reached **during** the trading day.
blocks.text: While the old "day trade count" is gone, the focus shifts to a more dynamic metric called the Intraday Margin Level (IML). Instead of checking account balances solely at end of day, the new rule requires monitoring of a customer account's highest margin deficiency reached during the trading day.

blocks.raw:
| Concept                         | Definition                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Standardized Minimum Equity** | All margin accounts are subject to a **$2,000 minimum equity requirement** (or 100% of the purchase price, whichever is less) |
| **Intraday Margin Level (IML)** | The amount of cash a customer could withdraw while still maintaining required maintenance margin                              |
| **Intraday Margin Deficit**     | Occurs when the IML becomes a **negative number** due to IML-reducing transactions                                            |

blocks.raw: ## Pattern day trader
blocks.text: Pattern day trader

blocks.raw: A user is marked as a Pattern Day Trader when they execute four or more day trades within a **rolling** five business day period in a margin account. Once marked as a PDT, the account must maintain a minimum equity balance of $25,000. If the equity falls below this threshold, any further attempts to day trade will be blocked until the required balance is restored.
blocks.text: A user is marked as a Pattern Day Trader when they execute four or more day trades within a rolling five business day period in a margin account. Once marked as a PDT, the account must maintain a minimum equity balance of $25,000. If the equity falls below this threshold, any further attempts to day trade will be blocked until the required balance is restored.

blocks.raw: An account that has been marked as a pattern day trader, will be restricted from day trading in the following scenarios:
blocks.text: An account that has been marked as a pattern day trader, will be restricted from day trading in the following scenarios:

blocks.raw:
1. If the account equity balance falls below $25K the account will be restricted at the end of the trading day
2. If a day trade is attempted and the equity balance is below $25K the account will be restricted immediately
blocks.text: If the account equity balance falls below $25K the account will be restricted at the end of the trading dayIf a day trade is attempted and the equity balance is below $25K the account will be restricted immediately

blocks.raw: An account that has been marked as a pattern day trader, will be allowed to continue or resume day trading in the following scenarios:
blocks.text: An account that has been marked as a pattern day trader, will be allowed to continue or resume day trading in the following scenarios:

blocks.raw: 1. If the account equity balance exceeds $25K, the account will be unrestricted after market close and able to day trade the next trading day
blocks.text: If the account equity balance exceeds $25K, the account will be unrestricted after market close and able to day trade the next trading day

blocks.raw: ### Impact of day trading restriction
blocks.text: Impact of day trading restriction

blocks.raw: If an account is restricted from day trading, orders will be rejected to prevent additional day trades from occurring.
blocks.text: If an account is restricted from day trading, orders will be rejected to prevent additional day trades from occurring.

blocks.raw: For example, if the account already purchased TSLA today, any new sell order of TSLA (market, limit, stop, etc.) will be rejected.
blocks.text: For example, if the account already purchased TSLA today, any new sell order of TSLA (market, limit, stop, etc.) will be rejected.

blocks.raw: Additionally, restricted accounts cannot have pending orders for the same symbol on opposite sides. For example, if an account has a pending sell limit order of ABC, any new buy order of ABC will be rejected, until the pending sell order has either been canceled or filled.
blocks.text: Additionally, restricted accounts cannot have pending orders for the same symbol on opposite sides. For example, if an account has a pending sell limit order of ABC, any new buy order of ABC will be rejected, until the pending sell order has either been canceled or filled.

blocks.raw:
> ❗️ Market risk in restricted accounts
>
> For accounts flagged as PDT with an equity balance below $25,000, same-day exits of newly established long positions are not permitted. To help customers avoid unintended market exposure and potential losses, it is recommended to issue a prompt or warning before a new purchase, since that instrument will be prohibited from sales for the remainder of the day.

blocks.raw: ## Good faith violations
blocks.text: Good faith violations

blocks.raw: In a cash Account, a customer can reinvest funds immediately after a sale. For example, imagine a customer has no cash in their Account, and then sells their stock:
blocks.text: In a cash Account, a customer can reinvest funds immediately after a sale. For example, imagine a customer has no cash in their Account, and then sells their stock:

blocks.raw:
```json
POST /back-office/orders 
{
  "accountNo": "DWPH000003",
  "orderType": "MARKET",
  "symbol": "AAPL",
  "side": "SELL",
  "clientNotes": "Manual limit order",
  "amountCash": 400,
}
```
This Account now has cash available to trade, but not to withdraw, and cash is pending settlement from this stock sale:
blocks.text: This Account now has cash available to trade, but not to withdraw, and cash is pending settlement from this stock sale:

blocks.raw: Every asset settles with a different time period. Equity sales, for example, settle 1 business day after the trade is executed.
blocks.text: Every asset settles with a different time period. Equity sales, for example, settle 1 business day after the trade is executed.

blocks.raw: By default, this customer is allowed to purchase more stock with this cash, even though it is pending settlement. However, if they do so, they may not sell the new Position before this cash settles. Doing so would be a Good Faith Violation and would be listed in the Violations endpoint:
